title: Conflict as an Inverse of Attention in Sequence Relationship
answer_short: Tasks involving non-duplicate or contrastive pairs where attention's bias toward similarity limits performance.
answer_rationale: The conflict method is tested on tasks where attention's bias toward similarity hinders performance, particularly in cases involving non-duplicate or contrastive pairs. Text 2 explicitly states that attention works best when there is a match between sequences but struggles with contrastive or non-similar pairs, which is where the conflict method is introduced to emphasize repelling relationships. Text 4 and Text 5 further support this by showing empirical gains in tasks where attention incorrectly marked pairs as duplicates but the conflict model correctly identified them as non-duplicates, especially in cases with minor differences.
